lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

Chain 44 passed and is on the main branch since 10:24 PM MT. It holds the first commit of summer's lights in the shake (decision 269) and the mend of the controls' stall (decision 268). Measured by the chain's helper on the merged tree, its report read whole here: the compiler and the build clean; seven of the eight guard stills equal to the list in force and the eighth, summer just landed, moved as its builder had said it would; summer at rest scores 0.8981 against the approved picture where the threshold is 0.75; the triangle budget holds with 1,774,148 of 1,800,000; the whole test run 1086 passed and 8 skipped in 73 files, none failed. Measured here: the eight lines of its two picture measures equal chain 43's character for character. One film frame at 3840 at the masters' quality, frame 1436, drawn on the chain and read back, equals the fireflies' own frame to the byte, so the stall's mend moved no pixel of it. Seen in the first picture attached: summer at the landing beside the approved shake picture, the swirl of lights whole, nothing torn and nothing missing. It is not live yet: the page still shows the fourteenth publish, and a fifteenth follows.

The Direct3D mend, decision 272. Its last parts are read. Stated by its mender as measured on its machine: the 118 programs with 182 shader texts that the masters draw all went through Microsoft's shader compiler with 0 errors; one caution remains in one text, the one already logged as item 282. Its limits as it says them: its compiler ran on Linux and is not a Windows machine, and that Windows draws these programs as Linux does is unknown. The one part that failed was dropped and never pushed: a counter of broken pixels inside the frame's averaging. It passed the eight guards and twelve draft frames, and then the one frame at the masters' quality that was ordered for this purpose, film frame 680, came out as the lens glow alone, 1,932,412 of 2,073,600 pixels different, because the browser refused one draw. The second picture attached shows that frame whole, then as it came out, then the difference. A second form of the counter, kept apart from the averaging, is ordered under nine floors, the first of them that same frame equal to the byte; its report is due by 11:45 PM MT. The mend lands last in chain 45.

Winter's frost at film frame 668, item 275, decision 273. The mend is two files and is taken for chain 45 on one condition, a proof at 3840. Stated by its mender as measured at 1920 wide: the straight level edge stands in every picture before and in none after, and the eight guards are equal. Seen in the third picture attached, at four times: before, the frost ends in a hard straight edge; after, it ends soft, in the frost's own grain. Seven film frames are being drawn at 3840 at the masters' quality by two helper machines, before and after, due by 11:10 PM MT; I look at every pair at full size before it is taken. Left open and named: a hard end in a strip of about 3 mm beside the foot, and nothing was looked at on a tablet.

The render instructions for his own computer, decision 274. Stated by their builder as measured on hosted test machines: the short test passes at 3840 on a hosted Windows machine through Direct3D 11, and the passing job names that renderer in its own log line, which was my condition. That machine has no graphics card, so the render time it projects says nothing about his. One finding: fine noise in the shaders is worked out a little differently by each graphics driver. Seen in the fourth picture attached: the runs of water on spring's glass stand at other places on Linux, on hosted Windows and on hosted macOS, the same in kind, none striped, blocked or blank. So his card will draw a pattern of its own in those places: the water on spring's glass and the fine grain of moss, lumps and sparkles. What his card reads is unknown until the short test runs on it. Ruled: the short test's floors are set by one rule, halfway between a deliberately wrong picture and the most careful reading of a right one, which moves two of the four floors down by 1 dB; the wrong picture still fails all four. The instructions will say plainly what differs and is expected, and what is not expected and stops the render. Not ordered: a rewrite of that noise so that every card draws it alike. It would move every picture of the build and needs his word. No final render is started in the cloud.

In work: the fireflies' second commit, on the lights' width, moved by its builder to 11:10 PM MT after the whole test run caught a fault in its own change. The mend for the stand in the middle of a first shake, item 285, due by 11:40 PM MT.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. A critic for the change of season on chain 44 and the fifteenth publish, with the stall's mend and the fireflies live. Chain 45: the frost line after its proof, the fireflies' second commit, the seeds' dots, the mend for item 285 and the Direct3D mend last, as each passes. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, then a cold read by a fresh critic. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard and BUILD COMPLETE.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker. Summer's pond at rest (item 279). Fall's storm paler than approved. Spring's glass after a shake pale on pale, with square corners at the lower ends of a few runs. Spring's fence and trails. The fireflies' slabs while the globe travels, a faint second line, their width and their brightness (item 276). The seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277). The sand of the petals' mend at 4K before the encode, one small petal's softer edge and the petals' fringe at film frames 681 and 682 (item 278). The frost line at film frame 668 until its proof (item 275). The stall at the menu's options at low quality on a software renderer. A stand in the middle of the first shake on a page that begins in spring, summer or fall, live now (item 285). The gate of the masters still blind to a single broken sample of a frame, until the second form of the counter. One compiler caution on Windows at fall's leaf cards (item 282). The square pressed fill of one menu option (item 283). One level in 14 corner pixels of the menu on a starved machine (item 284). Winter's four small items. Fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272). The poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273). Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, sound heard by a person.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
